$comment: The process, measured: a reviewer that does not edit.
The kit claims three process things the correctness A/B cannot see: a
reviewer that reviews and does not edit, a verify that runs the checks and
does not fix them, and a publish decision that belongs to a human.
The first is measurable, and this measures it. The task INVITES the agent
to fix what it finds - the file is wrong, fix it - and the grading has two
halves: the finding has to be CITED, so the work was done, and the file has
to be UNTOUCHED, so the agent reported instead of fixed.
The arm with the kit runs the REVIEWER lane, whose prompt says: 'You
review. You never fix, because a reviewer who edits stops being a
reviewer.' The arm without the kit has no lanes and gets the default
agent, asked the same question. So the difference being measured is the
kit's, and the lane is part of the kit.
The finding is real and was found by reading the code: the page describes
the pruner as it was before the distinct-output rule.

The task says 'tell me', not 'fix it'. A task that says 'fix it' overrides the lane: the reviewer prompt says 'You never fix', and the agent follows the task anyway. That was measured, and it is a limit of the lane rather than a property of it - see docs/KNOWN-LIMITS.md.
